videos.script: The bookshop is online, on HTTPS, with a real certificate. Now ask it a few questions a stranger would ask. {{stranger}} What software are you, and which version? It tells you, on every page. What do you serve when I ask by address? It serves the shop. Is there a copy of your source code lying around? There is. {{answers}} None of these is a break-in. Each one is a free answer to a question an attacker would otherwise have to work for. {{free}} This lesson closes them, one at a time, and checks each one from outside before and after. {{close}} You will hide the version, refuse names the server does not serve, and send the headers that tell a browser what to refuse. You will meet the configuration mistake that silently switches those headers off. {{headers}} Then limits: on methods, on how fast a client may ask, and on how slowly it may talk. And last, what the application could do if it were broken into, and how to make that very little. {{limits}}
